info_server: Enter the IP address or host name of your digitalSTROM server - only once: it applies to both interfaces the adapter uses.
help_host: IP address or hostname of the digitalSTROM server (port 8080 is used automatically)
label_validateCertificate: Validate TLS certificate of the DSS
help_validateCertificate: Only enable with a valid, non-self-signed certificate
info_token: The credentials (usually dssadmin - the same ones as for the dSS configurator) are used once to create the app token and are not stored. The instance has to be running for this.
help_appToken: Filled automatically when created - alternatively paste an existing app token here
help_dataPollInterval: Interval for polling meter data in seconds. Default 100s: a cycle reads two values per circuit, which keeps the adapter within the DSS rules 8/9 (at most one cyclic read per minute and circuit). Smaller values are allowed from 60s on but exceed that guideline. 0 disables polling.
help_deleteUnknownObjects: Warning: objects of temporarily unreachable devices are deleted too, including their history settings!
info_tls: A digitalSTROM server ships with a self-signed certificate, so the check is disabled by default. The connection is encrypted, but the adapter does not verify who it is talking to. Run the DSS and ioBroker in a trusted network segment, or use a host name with a valid certificate.
info_smartHome: Newer digitalSTROM servers offer a second, modern interface in addition. The adapter uses it as a turbo for reading: **all meter values and all output values** (brightness, blind positions, colour values) arrive in one single request each instead of many individual ones. The startup finishes in seconds instead of minutes, values are fresh again quickly after scene calls, and your dSS is noticeably relieved. **No separate key is needed for this** - the login from step 2 is enough. Should the Smart Home API ever not answer, the proven path takes over automatically.
label_useSmartHomeApi: Read meter and output values through the Smart Home API
help_useSmartHomeApi: Reads meter and output values bundled through the Smart Home API. Needs a dSS with firmware 1.19 or newer. Uses the login from step 2 - a separate key is optional.
help_smartHomeApiKey: Optional. Created from the existing app token, no password needed. Visible in the dSS under System > Access Authorization.
info_token_role: The app token is the adapter's base access: **button presses, sensor values and all events arrive through it in real time**, and **every switching command** runs over it. Nothing works without it - create it once with your dSS credentials.
section_status: Division of labour between the two interfaces
info_status: The adapter joins both interfaces of your dSS into one team and uses the strongest one for each task: real-time events and control through the app token, bundled values through the Smart Home API. This page shows live which path is doing the work.
status_not_running: The instance is not running right now - the live status appears as soon as it does.
status_events_help: Button presses, sensor values, binary inputs and every switching command - in real time
status_meters_help: Power and energy of every circuit
status_outputs_help: Brightness, blind positions and colour values of the devices
token_created: App token created and placed into the field below - press Save to store it permanently.
key_created: API key created and taken over - press Save to store it permanently.
info_why: Your digitalSTROM server offers two interfaces with different strengths - and this adapter deliberately uses both. The app token delivers **events in real time** (button presses, sensor values, binary inputs) and executes **every switching command**. The Smart Home API bundles **all meter and output values into one single request each**. Together this means: the adapter starts in seconds instead of minutes, values are fresh again quickly after scene calls, and your dSS carries noticeably less load - at full reliability, because should the Smart Home API ever not answer, the proven path takes over automatically. The Status tab shows which path is doing the work right now.
status_connection_help: Classic interface is reachable and logged in
status_notifications_help: dSS change notifications - reconciled at most every five minutes
info_apiKeyOptional: Normally there is nothing to enter here. The adapter signs in to the Smart Home API with the app token from step 2 as well. A separate key is still possible: it is **permanently valid** and **visible and revocable on its own** in the dSS under System > Access Authorization. Important: **save** the dialog after creating one - otherwise the running instance does not know the new key.
info_credentials: The app token from step 2 is the adapter’s identity - and it opens **both** interfaces. So the Smart Home API needs no second key; the adapter simply uses the login it has anyway. **This changes nothing about the division of labour**: events and switching commands keep running through the classic interface, bundled meter and output values through the Smart Home API. The status tab shows it unchanged. A separate API key stays possible and is then the preferred path - it is permanently valid and can be revoked on its own in the dSS. Should the dSS ever reject it (revoked, or replaced by a newer one of the same name), the adapter says so once in the log and carries on with the login.
warnLimit_info: The object warning limit sets the number of objects above which ioBroker warns about this instance: if the instance has **more objects than the limit** when it starts, js-controller writes a warning to the log and reports it as a notification of the host. It neither limits how many objects are created nor how they are displayed. A higher limit does not reduce memory usage.
warnLimit_manual: The limit can also be changed directly in ioBroker Admin: open "Objects", switch on expert mode, search for the state and change its **value** there - not the object definition (JSON), not common.def and not a file in the adapter directory.
warnLimit_source_none: No valid value in the instance state
warnLimit_default_version: Default of the installed adapter version {version}
warnLimit_copyFailed: Copying is not possible - please select the ID and copy it manually.
warnLimit_help_edit: A whole number without thousands separators, e.g. {example}. "Save" writes it to the state.
warnLimit_help_editNoExample: A whole number without thousands separators. "Save" writes it to the state.
warnLimit_help_locked: Cannot be changed while the state is missing or cannot be read.
warnLimit_input_notWholeNumber: Digits only - no dot, comma or space.
warnLimit_input_tooSmall: The limit has to be at least 1 - with 0 ioBroker warns on every start.
warnLimit_draft_pending: Not saved yet - click "Save" below. The new limit then applies from the next start of the instance.
warnLimit_draft_changedMeanwhile: The state has been changed to {value} in the meantime. "Save" still writes the value you entered.
warnLimit_save_failed: The object warning limit was not saved: {error}
warnLimit_save_permission: No write permission for the state - the object warning limit was not saved.
warnLimit_save_connection: No connection to ioBroker Admin - the object warning limit was not saved.
warnLimit_configError: Object warning limit: please enter a whole number of at least 1.
warnLimit_error_permission: No read permission for the state.
warnLimit_error_connection: No connection to ioBroker Admin - the value cannot be read right now.
warnLimit_error_other: The value could not be read: {error}
warnLimit_hint_stale: The connection to ioBroker Admin is interrupted - what is shown may be outdated.
warnLimit_hint_pending: Saved. js-controller takes the new limit over at the next start of the instance - until then nothing changes.
warnLimit_hint_differs: The configured warning limit differs from the adapter default.
warnLimit_hint_notPositive: With a limit of 0 or below, js-controller warns on every start as soon as the instance has any objects at all - 0 does not switch the warning off. **How to fix it:** enter a number of at least 1 below and save.
warnLimit_hint_fraction: The limit has decimal places. js-controller still compares against exactly this value.
warnLimit_hint_controllerTooOld: The installed js-controller {version} does not evaluate the limit - it does so from version {min} on.
warnLimit_hint_defaultIgnored: The installed js-controller {version} does not use the adapter default yet: newly created states get 5,000 with it. That changes from js-controller {min} on.
warnLimit_status_unsupported: The installed js-controller {version} has no object warning limit per instance. It exists from js-controller {min} on; until then ioBroker does not warn about this instance.
warnLimit_status_noObject: The state does not exist for this instance yet. js-controller creates it at the next start of the instance.
warnLimit_status_noObjectUnknownControll: The state does not exist for this instance. From js-controller {min} on the controller creates it when the instance starts; the installed controller version could not be determined.
warnLimit_status_noState: The state has no value yet. At the next start of the instance js-controller fills one in itself: the adapter default from js-controller 7.1.2 on, 5000 before.
warnLimit_status_empty: The state is empty. js-controller therefore uses its replacement value of {fallback} objects at the start. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_status_emptyUnknownFallback: The state is empty. js-controller therefore uses a built-in replacement value at the start. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_status_invalid: The state holds {raw} - but {type}, not as a number. js-controller only evaluates numbers and therefore uses its replacement value of {fallback} objects at the start. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_status_invalidUnknownFallback: The state holds {raw} - but {type}, not as a number. js-controller only evaluates numbers and therefore uses a built-in replacement value at the start. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_faq_must_q: Do I have to change the limit?
warnLimit_faq_must_a: No - it makes no difference to how the adapter works. If the instance has more objects than the limit - for example 6,000 objects with a limit of 5,000 - exactly one thing happens: on every start of the instance js-controller writes a warning to the log and reports it in ioBroker Admin under "Hosts". **All objects are created anyway and work normally** - nothing is missing, cut off or hidden. A higher limit is worth it when the number of objects fits your installation and the recurring warning bothers you.
warnLimit_faq_speed_q: Does it make digitalSTROM or ioBroker slower or faster?
warnLimit_faq_speed_a: No. The limit is only the threshold for a count js-controller makes at every start of the instance anyway - whatever value is set. **The adapter itself does not read the limit**: the connection to the dSS, polling intervals, scenes, devices and switching commands stay unchanged, and the dSS never learns about the limit.
warnLimit_faq_many_a: Many objects can affect the performance of ioBroker, and an unexpectedly high number often points to a misconfiguration or a bug - that is how js-controller explains the warning. But that depends on the objects themselves, not on the limit: **a different limit neither creates nor removes a single object.** A digitalSTROM installation quickly reaches several thousand objects, because the adapter creates scene states of their own for every device with an output and for every room. That is why this adapter suggests a higher default (see "Adapter default" above). If the number is far above what your installation would lead you to expect, the warning is a fair hint.
warnLimit_faq_value_a: Somewhat above the actual number of objects of this instance, for example the adapter default. That keeps the warning as a safeguard in case the number of objects ever grows unexpectedly. A very high number practically switches this safeguard off, and 0 does not switch the warning off but triggers it on every start. The warning in the log itself tells how many objects the instance has ("This instance has … objects") - it only appears, though, when the limit is exceeded.
warnLimit_faq_when_q: When does the change apply - and does the warning disappear then?
warnLimit_faq_when_a: The check runs **only when the instance starts**. A changed limit therefore applies from the next start - the instance is not restarted for it automatically. js-controller does not take back a notification it has already raised; acknowledge it in ioBroker Admin under "Hosts". If the number of objects is not above the new limit, it does not come back at the next start.
warnLimit_faq_scope_q: Does it affect other instances or adapters?
warnLimit_faq_scope_a: No. The limit only applies to this instance; other instances and adapters have their own. You can change it again at any time.
warnLimit_effective_fallback: Applies at the start: {value} - replacement value of js-controller
warnLimit_source_fallback: Replacement value of js-controller - the state holds no valid number
warnLimit_status_invalidPending: The state holds {raw} - but {type}, not as a number. js-controller only evaluates numbers: at the next start it therefore uses its replacement value of {fallback} objects and writes that number into the state. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_status_emptyPending: The state is empty. At the next start js-controller therefore uses its replacement value of {fallback} objects and writes that number into the state. **How to fix it:** enter the number you want below and save.
warnLimit_error_objectPermission: No read permission for the object definition of the state - it cannot be changed right now.
warnLimit_error_objectOther: The object definition of the state could not be read just now - it cannot be changed at the moment.
warnLimit_save_timeout: No answer from ioBroker Admin - it is unclear whether the object warning limit was saved. If the value arrives, this note disappears; otherwise check it with "Read again".
